misconceptions.label: Coordinates read in the wrong order
misconceptions.description: Takes the first number of a pair as the vertical coordinate.

refutation.text_md: You found the right two numbers.
A pair is written across first, then up: $(x, y)$.
Read the first number along the $x$-axis before you move up or down.

misconceptions.label: A negative coordinate plotted as positive
misconceptions.description: Uses the size of each coordinate but ignores its sign.

refutation.text_md: Your distances from the axes are right.
A minus sign sends you left or down.
Check each sign before you plot.

misconceptions.label: Stops at the sum of squares
misconceptions.description: Adds the squared differences and gives that as the distance.

refutation.text_md: Squaring and adding was the right start.
That sum is the distance squared.
Take its square root to finish.

misconceptions.label: Perpendicular gradients taken as parallel
misconceptions.description: Treats two gradients whose product is -1 as the mark of parallel lines.

refutation.text_md: You noticed the gradients are related.
A product of $-1$ is the sign of perpendicular lines.

misconceptions.label: Halves the difference instead of the sum
misconceptions.description: Subtracts the end points' coordinates before halving.

refutation.text_md: The mid-point averages the end points: add, then halve.
